sources.title: NKG / Aggarwal attachment appeals — 1 April 2026
sources.summary: Original tribunal order supplies procurement-document allegations, ED monetary decomposition, defendants’ objections and an attachment decision. It does not adjudicate criminal guilt.
limitations: Original PDF contains inconsistent lakh/crore units in §§ 8(ii), 20; use the exact rupee amount in § 27(b) with the mismatch disclosed.
The narrative sometimes says Jagdish Kumar Aggarwal where case context identifies Jagdish Kumar Arora, and alternates NKG Pvt. Ltd./Limited; no new person/company is created from those variants.
Allegations in a judicial container remain allegations; underlying ledgers/exhibits were not obtained.

sources.title: Tajinder Pal Singh — NKG recall application dismissed
sources.publisher: Delhi High Court; original judgment hosted by ED
sources.summary: Court recounts ECIR payment figures and dismisses NKG’s effort to recall the approver order. Cross-examination remains available at trial.
limitations: The payment and proceeds figures are expressly introduced as the ECIR account, not independently examined bank statements.
§ 2 describes an ECIR dated 6 July 2022; the older bail text distinguishes the CBI FIR dated 6 July from the ECIR dated 28 September 2022. This discrepancy is not silently normalized.
Integral is called both Ltd. and a proprietorship; the legal-form inconsistency does not justify a company/CIN merge.

sources.title: NKG Infrastructure Limited — Annual Report FY 2019–20
sources.locator: Printed pp 24, 31, 33, 54; original PDF pp 26, 33, 35, 56; MGT-9 and share-capital note
sources.summary: Company-published CIN, board roles and dated share-class ownership provide accountable corporate context. No flowmeter receipts can be attributed to shareholders from this report alone.

Equity percentages on printed p 54 use the equity-share denominator; promoter total-share percentages on p 33 include preference capital and differ legitimately.
